title: Empire State Manufacturing Survey, September 2026 — the half of the pair that actually closes the gap, 8:30 a.m. ET
source: EST: newyorkfed.org/survey/empire/empiresurvey_overview — the New York Fed's own Empire State Manufacturing Survey overview page, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 131,466 bytes) by this event's own never-assessed initial research, independently of the philly-fed-mfg-2026-09-17 sweep that proposed this entry the same day. Its 2026 release grid enumerates the full year verbatim — JAN 15 · FEB 17 · MAR 16 · APR 15 · MAY 15 · JUN 15 · JUL 15 · AUG 17 · SEP 15 · OCT 15 · NOV 16 · DEC 15 — above the page's own timing note 'Released at or shortly after 8:30 a.m.' Independently reproduced by the survey's published rule (the 15th of the month, rolled forward off weekends: Feb 15 2026 was a Sunday and the grid shows Feb 17, Aug 15 was a Saturday and the grid shows Aug 17); 2026-09-15 is a Tuesday, so no roll applies. Filed estimate on the two standing counts every sibling regional-survey entry documents, neither of which is doubt about the date: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no member for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule (FED: covers the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar only), and this lane does not self-confirm. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL entry written 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, which read the one proposal that existed for this id (proposals/empire-state-mfg-2026-09-15.from-philly-fed-mfg-2026-09-17.json) and re-verified its primary independently, as the proposal itself asked the canonical author to do. The proposal's coverage-gap argument stands unchanged: two open ledgers name this print as a decision input (empire-state-mfg-2026-10-15's kill-switch list and philly-fed-mfg-2026-10-15's This-week watch list) and the calendar tracked it nowhere. Initial research (docs/research/events/empire-state-mfg-2026-09-15.md) then measured three things no sibling had. FIRST, the Empire-Philly convergence the pair's three registered forward tests turn on is overwhelmingly an EMPIRE-side event, and only on prices paid. Regressing each bank's next-month prices-paid change on the current gap across the 302 months the surveys share (2001-07 to 2026-08): Empire's slope is -0.428 (t = -10.10), Philly's +0.120 (t = 2.22) — Empire's response is 3.6x larger and five times better determined. In the 17 prior instances of an absolute gap at or above today's 17.7, the Empire side supplied 181.2 of the 198.6 total points of closing against Philly's 17.4, and in the 16 with today's sign (Empire above Philly) Empire's prices paid fell the next month 13 of 16 times, median -12.0, against a median Philly change of +1.0. This is not a noise artifact: on the common window Empire's prices-paid index is the LESS volatile of the two (sd of monthly change 7.76 vs 8.61), so the reverting side is the steadier one. The same test on the headline is symmetric (Empire -0.394, Philly +0.316), so the asymmetry is a prices-paid property specifically. The operational consequence is that the 09-15 print, not the 09-17 one, most likely settles FT-philly-fed-mfg-2026-09-17-2 and the sibling's October convergence test. SECOND, the pair's disagreement is CROSSED and near-unprecedented: Empire's headline sits 26.8 points BELOW Philly's (the 2.0th percentile of the signed gap) while its prices paid sits 17.7 points ABOVE (the 94.4th). Both gaps at these magnitudes with opposite signs has happened in exactly 2 of 302 common months — 2026-08 and 2020-04, an unusable analogue. THIRD, the surveys' collection windows differ in a way that matters this month: the bank's own August note states 'Survey responses were collected between August 3 and August 10' against an August 17 release, putting September's collection at roughly Sep 1-8 — closing three days BEFORE the 09-11 CPI print and eight before the FOMC decision, where Philly's inferred Sep 7-14 window spans the CPI. Empire's September print is the pair's pre-CPI, pre-FOMC half. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the same grounds as every sibling regional-survey entry: a single-state qualitative diffusion index over roughly 100 respondents, no house playbook keyed to regional surveys, and no tracked name carrying a New York district manufacturing channel. What the entry buys is that the 09-15 morning is honestly counted — Empire's 8:30 slot is uncontested, the cleanest of the pair's three 2026 mornings — and that the convergence question gets adjudicated on the date the measurement says it actually resolves. This entry is an ESTIMATE, which widens caution and licenses nothing.
